Anatomy AI · iPhone & iPad
Privacy policy
Effective: 23 September 2026 · Applies to Anatomy AI version 1.0
Anatomy AI is an anatomy-learning application provided by Michael Harvey through Know & Guide. This policy describes the app's study features, optional connected teacher and support contact. Privacy questions can be sent to winseral@knowandguide.com.
At a glance: Study progress is stored on your device. Bundled lessons, quizzes and spoken explanations do not require an AI server. Questions go to an external teacher only when you configure a connection and give permission. Do not enter identifying client information or medical records.
1. Study information on your device
The app stores learning progress, bookmarks, reviewed steps, quiz and revision results, review dates, completed fictional-case identifiers, preferences and the last selected study area. It also stores your teacher choice, optional backend address and permission receipt. A backend access token is held in the iOS Keychain; an AI provider API key is not bundled in the app.
These records provide study and connection features. They are not automatically uploaded as a student profile. Device backups may include app data according to your Apple settings. Exported progress files go to a location or service you choose. Teacher chat text and client worksheet text are not written into the app's progress backup.
2. Offline teaching, Apple AI and narration
The offline guide uses bundled material. On supported devices, the Apple on-device teacher processes a question locally to select a lesson topic; the app supplies authored learning text. These modes do not send your question to a Know & Guide teacher server.
Lesson narration uses Apple's system speech synthesis and bundled scripts. The app does not record microphone audio or implement camera, contacts, location or HealthKit access. System keyboard dictation and Apple service features are governed by your device settings and Apple's policies.
3. Optional connected teacher
Version 1.0 does not ship with a preconfigured hosted teacher address. You can configure a compatible backend and approve that destination. When you send a connected question, the app sends your question, recent conversation, selected lesson or structure, learning context and any scenario text included with the request. Anything you type, including health-related information, may be transmitted; the app's warning is not automatic redaction.
The backend receives authentication and network information needed to serve the request. The supplied reference backend forwards the teaching request to OpenAI. A custom backend may use different operators or providers: verify the actual recipient, hosting location, privacy notice and retention arrangements before connecting. Do not approve an unknown service. The app's permission receipt is tied to the destination, named provider and notice version.
A connection test sends your access token to the configured backend, but not a study question. Switching back to the offline guide or revoking permission stops future teacher-question transfers; it does not undo requests already sent.
4. Retention and third-party processing
Local progress and preferences: retained until reset, removed or replaced by you. Backups and exports have their own retention settings.
Teacher conversations: held in app memory while the teacher sheet is active, not deliberately persisted as chat history by this app. Your explicit sharing can create a separate copy.
Reference backend: does not implement a conversation database or write prompts and replies to application logs. Requests are processed in memory; access tokens and in-memory usage limits support authentication and rate limiting. A hosting service or modified backend can have additional logs and retention.
OpenAI: the reference backend uses store: false for response application state. This does not disable all provider logging. OpenAI documents default abuse-monitoring retention of up to 30 days, with stated exceptions and account-specific controls. See OpenAI API data controls.
External services may process information outside your country. There is no blanket zero-retention or healthcare-compliance promise. Ask the configured backend's operator about its actual host, processing countries, retention and deletion procedure. This website is not an AI backend and publishing this policy does not activate a connected teacher service.
5. Your choices, access and deletion
In the app's Settings you can export or reset learning progress, revoke connected-teacher permission, or remove the saved backend address and token. Deleting the app does not reliably remove Keychain records or copies held in system backups. Use the remove-connection control before uninstalling to clear the saved token. Delete exported files and backups separately through their storage providers.
For access, correction, deletion or a privacy complaint relating to information you supplied to Know & Guide, email the contact below. For information sent to another backend, contact that operator; we cannot directly erase records in an independently operated service. Do not include passwords, access tokens or client medical records in a request.
6. Support messages, this website and sharing
If you email us, we receive the contact details, message, device information and attachments you choose to send. We use them to answer your request, investigate faults or content concerns and keep the relevant correspondence. Retention depends on the unresolved support issue and any applicable record-keeping requirements; you may request deletion. Email-provider handling and backups are separate from the app's local storage.
These privacy and support pages are static pages hosted through GitHub Pages. The host can process normal website requests and technical data, including IP addresses, under the GitHub privacy statement. These two pages include no analytics scripts, advertising, forms, external fonts or tracking cookies of their own.
The app includes no advertising or analytics SDK. Opening an external link or using the share sheet sends you to a service you choose, whose own privacy terms apply. App distribution and Apple-managed diagnostics are subject to your Apple settings and Apple's policies.
7. Sensitive information and younger learners
Anatomy AI is a study aid, not a client-record system, diagnostic service or emergency service. Use fictional or de-identified study examples. Younger learners should use the app with suitable adult or instructor guidance and should not put personal information into teacher questions or support messages. Contact us about information sent in error.
8. Policy changes
Updates to this policy will appear here with a revised effective date. Material changes to connected processing require updated disclosures and, where appropriate, renewed permission. Details of any future Know & Guide hosted teacher must be disclosed before that service is enabled.

resources.text:
Anatomy AI · iPhone & iPad
Support for your studies
Version 1.0 · Updated 23 September 2026
Get help with anatomy exploration, narrated Movement and Massage lessons, quizzes, fictional case studies and the teacher connection.
Contact support
Michael Harvey · Know & Guide
winseral@knowandguide.com
Email Anatomy AI support
This opens your email application; no support form or account is required. This mailbox is not an emergency or clinical advice service.
Report a technical or content problem
Please include the app version and build shown in Settings, your iPhone or iPad model, iOS version, the body region and activity, and the steps that produced the problem. For narration or anatomy errors, include the structure, frame or question and a short description of the suspected error.
Screenshots are useful after removing personal details. Do not send client names, medical records, passwords, AI provider keys or backend access tokens. Avoid relying on disputed content until it has been checked with a qualified instructor.
No sound during a lesson
Open Move or Massage, select a frame and press Play or Replay this explanation.
Check that spoken explanations are enabled in Playback and voice settings and that an available English voice is selected.
Check media volume and the current speaker, headphones or Bluetooth output. Lesson audio pauses when the app is interrupted, leaves the foreground or opens the teacher.
Return to the lesson and press Play again. The app avoids unexpected automatic resumption after interruptions.
The lesson transcript remains available without sound. Narration uses the device's system voice and does not require a connected AI backend or microphone permission. Images are illustrated teaching sequences, not recorded practitioner videos.
Choosing a teacher
Offline study guide: uses bundled study material and works without a server; it is not a language model.
Apple on-device teacher: depends on supported Apple Intelligence hardware and an available system model. It helps choose the relevant authored study topic. If unavailable, select the offline guide.
Connected teacher: needs a compatible HTTPS backend, a separate app access token and your permission to send a question. Version 1.0 has no preconfigured hosted teacher address. Do not enter your provider API key into the app. Check the server operator's privacy details before approving it. A connection test checks access; it does not establish medical accuracy.
If a connected request fails, check the address, app access token and server availability, or use the offline guide. Do not send credentials to support. Starting a different backend connection requires renewed permission.
Progress, backups and privacy
Settings includes progress export and restore, progress reset, connected-teacher permission revocation and removal of the stored backend connection. Export important progress before resetting or replacing the app. Resetting does not delete previously exported files or device backups.
Use the remove-connection control before uninstalling to delete the saved access token. Removing a connection does not erase information already sent to a server. For privacy, access, correction or deletion requests relating to Know & Guide, email winseral@knowandguide.com. A separately operated backend must handle requests about data it holds.
Read the privacy policy
Learning and safety
Anatomy AI supports study and fictional case reasoning. It does not diagnose, prescribe treatment, certify hands-on competence or clear a real client for massage. Practical techniques require qualified instruction and appropriate consent. The current generated artwork and markers remain subject to anatomical review. For a real medical concern, consult an appropriate health professional; for an emergency, use your local emergency service.

White paper / Research proposal
AUM Acoustic Modulation and the Question of Extra Dimensions
Could a sustained chant reshaped by rotating blades tell us something new about sound and our experience of reality?
Michael Harvey | 19 September 2026 | Version 1.0
Exploratory proposal. The possible connection to extra dimensions is a conjecture. The paper sets out what can be measured acoustically and what further evidence a broader claim would require. No experiment has yet been performed for this proposal.
Download the white paper PDFFull paper also available below
The proposalWhat existing research establishesAn ordinary acoustic modelQuestions and evidence thresholdsA practical first experimentAnalysis and decisionsReferences and publication notes
The proposal
Abstract. This paper asks whether a sustained AUM chant, altered by rotating blades and airflow, could provide a useful starting point for investigating a possible connection to extra spatial dimensions. The motivating idea is speculative. No experiment has yet been performed for this proposal, and no evidence of such a connection is presented. The immediately testable part is the acoustic effect: how the recorded sound changes with fan speed, airflow and enclosure geometry.
The proposed programme begins with controlled, modest-volume recordings and comparisons against ordinary humming, pure tones and digitally modulated sound. A successful first study would characterise repeatable changes and establish how well standard acoustics explains them. An extra-dimensional interpretation would require a separate physical mechanism, quantitative predictions and independent evidence that these acoustic tests alone cannot supply.
Origin of the question
During meditation, I remembered speaking into a fan as a child and hearing my voice change. I wondered what would happen if I sustained AUM into a much larger moving-air system. Could the repeating interruption or reshaping of the sound reveal something about vibration and our experience of reality? If additional dimensions exist, could there be a physical connection worth investigating?
For me, AUM carries spiritual significance and invites reflection on the relationship between sound and life. That meaning motivates the question. The experimental proposal below addresses what instruments could measure, while leaving the broader spiritual interpretation open as a personal perspective.
Central proposition
Speculative proposition: if an additional physical degree of freedom exists and couples to matter or pressure fluctuations, a deliberately structured acoustic field might, in principle, influence or reveal that coupling. This paper does not establish either condition. It specifies the ordinary acoustic investigation that would have to come first.
Status: independent concept paper and proposed protocol; not peer reviewed. No experimental results, clinical benefits, communication with other realms or new physical mechanism are claimed.
What existing research establishes
Extra dimensions have a specific physical meaning
Everyday physics uses three spatial dimensions and time. Some physical theories propose additional spatial dimensions. CERN describes ways their effects might be sought through particle signatures and missing momentum in high-energy experiments [1]. A hypothetical extra spatial dimension is not automatically a parallel universe, a spiritual realm or a state of consciousness. These meanings need separate definitions.
The existence of an additional dimension would not by itself imply that audible sound can access it. A connection would require a defined interaction, an accessible scale and a measurable consequence. None is supplied by the analogy between vibration and the structure of reality.
AUM is a changing vocal sound
Voiced sound contains a fundamental frequency and harmonics; the vocal tract changes their relative strength [2]. For this protocol, AUM means a recorded progression through an open vowel, a rounded vowel and a closed-mouth hum. Actual pronunciation varies. There is no single pitch inherent in every AUM recording, so the experiment measures the source rather than assigning it a universal frequency.
Fans and enclosures alter sound
Related NASA engineering work studies acoustic transmission through a ducted fan [3]. A separate large-tunnel study measured sound pressure and structural vibration [4]. These provide context for blade scattering, machine noise and enclosure effects. Neither study tests AUM or a connection to extra dimensions. A household fan and a wind tunnel also differ in geometry, airflow and acoustic treatment, so scaling up does not guarantee a stronger version of the childhood effect.
Patterns and personal experience need separate interpretation
Harvard demonstrates how sand collects at relatively stationary nodes on a vibrating plate [5]. Such Chladni patterns show the behaviour of a resonating surface. Their symmetry is not evidence that sound has created life or opened another dimension.
A 2011 pilot fMRI study of 12 healthy volunteers compared OM chanting, an “ssss” task and rest. It reported reduced activity in several brain regions during OM relative to rest. Its proposed vagal explanation was preliminary, and relaxation remained a possible explanation [6]. This does not demonstrate extra-dimensional perception or a benefit from fan-modified chanting.
Search scope. Targeted searches for AUM or OM chanting combined with wind tunnels and fans did not locate a directly matching documented experiment. This was a targeted review, not a systematic review or proof that nobody has tried it. Sources were checked on 19 September 2026.
An ordinary acoustic model
Sound in air is a mechanical pressure disturbance. For a first approximation, a rotating fan can vary how much of the source sound is reflected or transmitted toward a microphone. This can produce periodic changes in the received amplitude. Moving blades can also change phase and frequency; airflow, turbulence and motor noise add further effects. The balance depends on placement and geometry.
For N equally spaced blades turning at R revolutions per minute, the blade-passage rate is:
f_b = N R / 60
A three-blade fan at 600 rpm has a blade-passage rate of 30 Hz. That is a timing calculation, not a prediction that every recording will contain one clean 30 Hz component. Blade shape, direct sound, reflections and the fan itself affect what is recorded.
A deliberately simplified amplitude-modulation model is:
y(t) = [1 + m cos(2 pi f_b t)] x(t)
Here x(t) is the original sound, y(t) is the altered sound and m is the modulation depth between 0 and 1. Multiplying a 200 Hz pure tone by a 30 Hz modulation envelope produces components at 170, 200 and 230 Hz. These extra components, called sidebands, follow directly from multiplying two periodic signals. They do not require new physics.
Figure 1. Illustrative calculation with modulation depth m = 0.6. Normalised units. Not experimental data.
An AUM recording contains many changing components, so its spectrum will be more complex. A long enclosure can also favour certain frequencies. The model above is a useful baseline, not a complete model of any fan or tunnel. An engineering model would include propagation, reflections, scattering and measured noise.
Questions and evidence thresholds
Separate three questions
Question
Operational test
What the result could establish
Acoustic change
Repeat identical source playback at measured fan speeds and compare spectra and timing.
A repeatable effect of the apparatus on recorded sound.
AUM specificity
Compare AUM with matched humming, vowels, tones and a synthetic harmonic sound.
Whether differences remain after specified acoustic features are controlled.
Extra-dimensional coupling
Requires a physical interaction model with a unique quantitative prediction.
Not established by the proposed audio experiment alone.
Working hypotheses
H0, ordinary acoustics: observed differences are consistent with source variation, periodic scattering or modulation, airflow, room or duct resonance, fan noise and measurement uncertainty.
H1, unexplained acoustic residual: a specified measurement departs reproducibly from the preselected baseline model and its uncertainty. This would first indicate that the model or apparatus needs investigation. It would not identify an extra dimension as the cause.
Hextra, the broader conjecture: an additional spatial degree of freedom couples to the acoustic system. In its current form this has no specified coupling law, predicted signal size or distinctive signature. It therefore cannot yet be discriminated from other explanations by this experiment.
What would make the broader claim testable
A future model would have to specify what quantity couples to the proposed dimension, why the chosen frequencies and geometry matter, and a prediction that standard acoustics does not make. It must also describe an outcome that would count against the model. A new spectral line, strong bodily sensation, unusual pattern or unexplained microphone signal is insufficient on its own.
If “connection” means transferring information, the claim additionally needs a defined sender, receiver and channel, a concealed random message, a predeclared scoring rule and controls against ordinary information leakage. The present proposal supplies none of those mechanisms and should not be described as a communication experiment.
A null result would constrain effects detectable with the stated apparatus and settings. It would neither disprove all extra-dimensional theories nor settle the personal spiritual meaning of AUM.
A practical first experiment
Apparatus and source preparation
Use a loudspeaker, an intact guarded variable-speed household fan, a microphone on a stand, a recorder with manual gain and a non-contact tachometer if available. Start without a tunnel. Keep the microphone outside the direct air jet and record positions, distances, fan orientation and room layout. Use normal comfortable listening levels; do not remove guards or place the face, hair or loose material near the blades. Large wind-tunnel work belongs in an operated facility.
Make one 10-second AUM recording and reuse the identical file. Prepare a sustained hum and vowel near its median fundamental pitch, a pure tone at that pitch, and a synthetic harmonic signal with a broadly similar spectrum. Match playback RMS level and document duration and spectral differences. No single control can match every feature of a changing chant.
Condition
Purpose
A Room only
Measure ambient and recorder noise with source and fan off.
B Source only
Establish each source spectrum with fan stationary in place.
C Fan only
Record fan sound at each selected speed without playback.
D Source plus fan
Measure the combined sound at the same speeds.
E Digital modulation
Replay a digitally modulated source with the fan off.
F Airflow without blades in the sound path
Later apparatus comparison using a remote blower and measured airflow.
Condition F is optional in the household pilot. A remote-blower arrangement changes the acoustic path and has its own noise, so it needs a fresh source-only and blower-only baseline. It approximates an airflow comparison; it does not perfectly isolate one variable.
Repeatable acquisition
Choose three fan settings and measure rpm where possible. Capture at least five trials per source and setting in randomised order, over two sessions. Record source-only trials and fan-only trials throughout the sessions to reveal drift. Allow fan speed to stabilise. This is an engineering pilot, not a statistical power calculation for a new physical effect.
Use uncompressed WAV at 48 kHz and 24 bit where supported. Disable automatic gain, voice isolation and noise suppression; avoid clipping. Keep playback level, gain and geometry fixed. If only a phone is available, record its model and app and treat hidden processing as a limitation. Save unprocessed files, timestamps, source identifiers, rpm, temperature where available and notes for every trial.
Analysis and decisions
Declare the comparison before collecting data
For the pure-tone control, use source-referenced sideband power near f0 plus and minus the measured blade-passage rate as the primary acoustic outcome. Before the main run, define frequency windows using recorder resolution and measured speed variation. Report fan-only power in those windows and the distribution across repeated trials. Without a tachometer, predictions based only on low, medium and high settings are less precise.
For AUM, use fixed time windows corresponding to its vowel and humming portions. Compare spectra and amplitude envelopes within the same windows across conditions. Use identical analysis settings for all trials. A spectrogram with a 4096-sample Hann window and 75 percent overlap at 48 kHz is one reasonable starting point; its frequency-bin spacing is about 11.7 Hz, so it will not resolve every closely spaced feature. Longer windows improve frequency resolution at the expense of time resolution.
Treat lower sidebands, higher sidebands, harmonics and noise separately. Preserve level information in the primary analysis; normalised plots may be added for shape comparisons if clearly labelled. A separately recorded fan trace is generally not phase-aligned with the fan during source playback. Subtracting its waveform does not reliably remove fan noise. Use it to characterise background variability and investigate uncertain results.
Investigate residuals in a defined order
First check clipping, automatic processing, fan-speed drift, electrical pickup and microphone wind sensitivity. Next repeat at another microphone position and with a second recorder where possible. Compare the physical fan condition with digital modulation, then assess enclosure resonance and mechanical vibration. Test promising effects on a later day before revising the physical explanation.
Keep any listening or meditation study separate from the acoustic pilot. If people compare recordings, randomise labels and order, match listening levels, and record prior expectations. Ratings of calmness, intensity or felt connection describe experience; they do not identify the physical origin of that experience.
Decision after the pilot
If modulation and ordinary acoustics explain the recordings, publish that useful result with the limits of the model. If a residual survives checks, report its magnitude, uncertainty and all conditions, then seek independent replication and acoustic expertise. A larger tunnel is justified only by a specific measurement question that the smaller setup cannot answer.
Conclusion. The original intuition can become a careful investigation of sound, airflow and perception. The proposed work can test repeatable acoustic behaviour. A connection to extra dimensions remains a conjecture requiring its own mechanism and distinctive evidence; a compelling sound or meaningful meditation experience does not establish that connection.
References and publication notes
[1] CERN. Extra dimensions gravitons and tiny black holes. Institutional explanation of hypothetical extra dimensions and possible particle-physics tests. It provides no proposed connection through audible chanting.
Open source
[2] UNSW Music Acoustics. Voice Acoustics an introduction. Research-group explanation and demonstrations of vocal sound production, harmonics and the filtering action of the vocal tract.
Open source
[3] Ed Envia, NASA, 2016. Acoustic Power Transmission Through a Ducted Fan. Related engineering research on sound transmission through a rotating ducted fan. This is not an experiment with AUM or extra dimensions.
Open source
[4] NASA, 1974. Acoustic measurement study 40 by 80 foot subsonic wind tunnel. Report NASA-CR-137573 describes measurements of sound pressure and structural vibration in and around a large wind tunnel.
Open source
[5] Harvard Natural Sciences Lecture Demonstrations. Chladni Plates. Demonstration of sand accumulating at the nodes of a vibrating plate.
Open source
[6] Kalyani BG and colleagues, 2011. Neurohemodynamic correlates of OM chanting. International Journal of Yoga 4(1), 3-6. doi:10.4103/0973-6131.78171. Pilot fMRI study with 12 healthy volunteers.
Open source
Author and scope
Michael Harvey, Know & Guide. Original concept from a meditation reflection and childhood experience of speaking into a fan. Research synthesis, drafting and formatting prepared with AI assistance. Author attribution identifies the originator of the proposal; it does not imply institutional affiliation or specialist validation.
Version 1.0, 19 September 2026. The equations and plotted example are illustrative calculations. No data were collected for this paper. This document is a research proposal, not a report of demonstrated extra-dimensional contact.

Balancing skills so upgrades actually feel different

iPhone & iPad game in development Aussie Backyard Games Pool whirlpools, clothesline chaos, soap slopes and the games we made up outside.
Rebuilding Australian Backyard Games for iPhone and iPad
Updated: September 1, 2026 • Category: iOS Game Development
Current status: actively in development.
Aussie Backyard Games is not yet an App Store release. The current build is being developed and play-tested as a collection of linked mini-games with persistent skills, unlockable items and a shared Backyard hub.
A lot of childhood games never had a board, a rulebook or even an agreed name. They were things kids invented because there was a swimming pool, a clothesline, a hose, a slippery patch of grass, a backyard and enough time to turn ordinary objects into a competition.
Aussie Backyard Games is an attempt to turn that memory into a playful iPhone and iPad game. The design is deliberately physical and slightly ridiculous. Rather than recreating polished organised sports, the mini-games are about momentum, timing, balance, strength, stamina, wind, water and the sort of rules that would have been negotiated five seconds before somebody yelled, “Go!”
The important part is the memory, not perfect simulation.
The game should feel like kids discovering what can be done with the backyard around them. The physics can be exaggerated, the scoring can be competitive and the characters can be silly, but each mini-game should still be recognisable as something that could have started with a group of kids and no equipment designed for the purpose.
The current backyard
🌊Whirlpool PoolRun around the pool to build a whirlpool, fight or use the current, push off the side, use floaties and weights, shove nearby players and try to stay in control as the water becomes increasingly chaotic.
👕Clothesline HoistUse strength and timing against a spinning clothesline, changing wind and flying clothes. Better pegs, clothing and persistent stamina change how long a player can hold on and how much chaos the line creates.
🧼Soap SlopeBuild speed, belly-flop before the line and slide as far as possible down a wet soapy slope. The camera follows the kid down the run while distance markers show whether the latest attempt beats the previous one.
A shared Backyard instead of separate apps
The mini-games live inside a central Backyard hub. Leaving a game returns the player to the Backyard, and progress carries between activities. The store is also shared so the player can see owned gear, persistent skills and upgrades rather than starting from zero every time a different backyard game is selected.
Persistent strength & staminaSkills matter across games and are intended to visibly change how long a kid can hold on, run or resist forces.
Unlockable gearFloaties, weights, clothes, pegs and other backyard objects can change a mini-game without turning it into a complicated inventory simulator.
Physical touch controlsTwo-finger running, holds, taps, swipes and contextual controls are designed around what the kid is actually doing in each game.
Readable mobile UIButtons, labels, score panels and store cards are being repeatedly adjusted so they remain readable on different iPhone and iPad screen sizes.
Kid-like physicsCharacters can be flung, dragged by water, slide awkwardly and recover. The animation does not need to look like professional sport.
Room to growThe Backyard structure makes it possible to add more remembered games later without rebuilding the whole app around each new idea.
Why the UI work matters as much as the physics
Much of the recent work has been less glamorous than adding a new mini-game: shrinking oversized store icons, increasing small item descriptions, improving text contrast, keeping Done and Backyard buttons away from the bottom edge, moving distance meters where the player can actually see them, and checking that controls stay on-screen across devices.
That iteration matters because these games are supposed to feel immediate. If a player has to hunt for the exit button or cannot read what an upgrade does, the simple backyard idea gets buried under interface friction.
Balancing skills so upgrades actually feel different
Strength and stamina are intended to change more than a number in a store. A higher stamina level should create a visibly larger or more capable stamina reserve; greater strength should slow stamina loss in strength-heavy games; AI kids need their own working stamina logic instead of being thrown from a clothesline while their bar appears frozen.
Those systems are still being tuned. The aim is for progression to make the player feel more capable while leaving enough unpredictability that a backyard game can still produce a ridiculous loss.
What comes next
The immediate work is continued polishing of the existing mini-games, controls, camera behaviour, physics and shared UI. After that, the Backyard can expand with more remembered games and variations.
This is one of the projects where the development process is part of the point: take a very personal memory, reduce it to the few mechanics that made it fun, then use iPhone and iPad hardware to make it playable again without making it too clean or too serious.

Agentic Coding Penpal
A Compassionate AI Tutor
A unique educational web application designed to be more than just a coding tool—it's a supportive friend. Built to reduce loneliness and foster creativity, it explains concepts and provides code snippets in the chat, encouraging you to "learn by doing".
Try the Penpal
What is it?
The Agentic Coding Penpal is built to reduce loneliness and foster creativity. It pairs students with a "compassionate AI companion" that teaches them how to code in real-time using voice and text.
Unlike standard code generators that do the work for you, the Penpal operates in "Tutor Mode". It acts as a guide, explaining concepts and providing code snippets in the chat, encouraging the student to type the code themselves. It then "reads" the student's work to verify correctness and offer specific, encouraging feedback.
Key Features
🗣️
Real-Time Voice
Talk naturally with the AI using Google's Gemini Multimodal Live API. It feels like a real conversation, not a command line.
👩‍🏫
Tutor Mode
The AI provides code snippets (Markdown) in the chat window, explaining why the code works before asking you to try it.
👁️
Smart Verification
The AI can "see" your code editor. After you finish typing, it inspects your work to ensure it's correct and helps you debug typos.
🎨
Multi-Language
Build projects in Python, C++, and Web (HTML/CSS/JavaScript). A versatile environment for any learner.
😊
Compassionate Persona
Programmed to be warm, playful, and patient, celebrating small wins to build your confidence as you learn.
Technical Highlights
Frontend
React, Vite, Tailwind CSS for a modern, responsive UI.
AI Core
Google Gemini Multimodal Live API via WebSocket for low-latency voice/video.
Infrastructure
Dockerized and deployed on Google Cloud Run for scalability.
Why "Tutor Mode"?
In early versions, the AI acted as a "Driver," writing code directly into the editor. However, we found that true learning happens when the student drives.
"We pivoted to Tutor Mode (v5.1), where the AI guides and verifies, ensuring students build actual muscle memory and understanding."

resources.text:
The Luminous Connection
Building a Modern E-Mobility Service Between Spiritual Centers and Travelers
Target Location: The Isha Foundation Area, India
⚡️ Introduction: Bridging the Gap Between Spirit and Modern Convenience
For spiritual travelers, retreat seekers, and pilgrims, the journey itself is often part of the experience. In destinations rich with ancient wisdom, like the grounds surrounding the Isha Foundation, the challenge isn't spiritual; it's logistical. Moving reliably, safely, and quickly between accommodation (motels) and the center itself can be a struggle.
We identified a critical gap: the need for a seamless, modern, and low-stress transportation solution. This leads us to propose The Luminous Connection—a premium, dedicated electric scooter shuttle service connecting local accommodations directly to the temple grounds.
🎯 The Opportunity: A Highly Defined Niche
Market Size: Defined by the steady flow of spiritual tourists and devotees (a consistent, repeatable clientele).
Value Proposition: We offer reliability, convenience, and comfort without the stress of cars, parking, or navigating unfamiliar, sometimes uneven terrain.
Revenue Model: We will utilize a Pass/Subscription Model (e.g., 'Daily Visitor Pass' or 'Weekend Retreat Package'), which guarantees predictable revenue streams by securing deals with the participating hotels and the Foundation.
📐 The Master Plan: Launching The Luminous Connection
Our strategy is not to scale immediately, but to validate and perfect. We follow a three-phase approach:
Phase 1: Proof of Concept (0–3 Months)
Goal: Prove demand and map the operational bubble.
Action: Secure cornerstone partnerships with 2-3 key motels and the Isha Foundation administration.
Fleet: Start incredibly small—3 to 5 scooters. This minimizes risk and allows us to perfect our operations.
Tech: Basic GPS tracking linked to a simple booking system (initially, a highly managed WhatsApp or Google Form booking system is sufficient).
Validation: Prove that 100% of scooters are utilized during peak hours.
Phase 2: Optimization and Scaling (4–12 Months)
Goal: Professionalize the service and expand coverage.
Action: Sign up a second tier of motel partners and establish reliable, commercial charging infrastructure at the motel hub.
Fleet: Scale based on utilization data (e.g., increase to 15–25 scooters).
Technology: Develop a dedicated, branded mobile application for booking, real-time tracking, and payment.
Operational Excellence: Hire and train local staff dedicated to fleet management and customer service.
Phase 3: Market Leadership (1+ Year)
Goal: Become the established, recognized backbone of mobility in the area.
Action: Explore integrating related services (e.g., luggage transfers, basic guide services).
🛴 Logistics and Operation Deep Dive
1. Hardware: The E-Scooters
Requirement: The scooters must be durable, reliable, and best suited for the terrain (handling slight inclines, varied paving, and monsoon conditions).
Mandatory Feature: Every single unit must be equipped with a high-grade, tamper-proof GPS tracker linked to a central, dedicated fleet management software (IoT platform).
2. Charging & Maintenance
Strategy: Centralized charging hub at the partner motel.
Resilience: Given potential local power fluctuations, the charging station must be equipped with reliable backup power (e.g., a small generator or battery bank) to ensure the fleet is always operational.
Support: A permanent local mechanic relationship is critical.
3. Technology Architecture (The App)
The app needs three pillars:
Customer View: Simple booking, real-time scooter location, payment gateway integration.
Admin/Staff View: Dashboard displaying the real-time status of every scooter (charging, available, in use, reported damage).
Management View: Handles bookings, payment reconciliation, maintenance scheduling, and generates reports for scaling decisions.
📜 Critical Considerations: Legal, Costing, & Partnerships
(Disclaimer: Consult a local Indian legal expert immediately.)
A. ⚖️ Legal & Regulatory Compliance (Non-Negotiable)
Permits: We must obtain all municipal permits for commercial e-mobility operations in the target area.
Insurance: Comprehensive commercial insurance covering theft, accident liability, and passenger injury is mandatory.
Local Rules: Understand local regulations regarding speed limits, designated paths, and licensed operations.
B. 💰 Supplier Sourcing and Costing (Next Steps)
Sourcing Strategy: Do not buy from a distant international supplier for the launch. Focus on established Indian e-mobility distributors who can provide local support, spare parts, and servicing.
Costing Breakdown (To be finalized by supplier quotes):
Scooter Units (3-5): Cost per unit + GST.
GPS Tracking/IoT: Cost per unit/month for tracking services.
Infrastructure: Cost for charging banks, security fencing, and local electrical work.
Working Capital: Funds needed for the first 3 months.
Shipping: Since we are focusing on a local launch, the shipping is minimal (local delivery of the units).
C. 🤝 Partnership Management
The relationship with the Motel must be formalized with a revenue-sharing agreement. They provide the captive market and the charging hub; we provide the service.
The relationship with the Isha Foundation must be built on respect, utility, and alignment with their mission.
🏁 Conclusion: From Idea to Impact
The Luminous Connection is more than a ride; it's a seamless piece of modern visitor infrastructure.
By focusing on a small, highly contained, and deeply valuable niche, we mitigate risk while building towards a profitable, impactful service that truly enhances the spiritual visitor experience.

headings: Paper Fleet Duel Has Become FlickFleet — Now on the App Store
What changed on the way to release
Recreating the biro flick on a touchscreen
Progression without losing the original game
An AI captain that is allowed to miss
From prototype tests to a released iPhone game
The name changed; the idea did not

From paper prototype to App Store release Paper Fleet Duel → FlickFleet Now available for iPhone on the Apple App Store
Paper Fleet Duel Has Become FlickFleet — Now on the App Store
Updated: August 13, 2026 • Category: Game Development / App Store Release
FlickFleet is now available on the Apple App Store.
The project developed under the working name Paper Fleet Duel. Its public App Store name is FlickFleet, with App Store version 1.0 approved for iOS.
Download FlickFleet on the App Store Support
Paper Fleet Duel began with a game I remember playing using nothing more than an A4 sheet of paper and a biro. We drew a line through the middle of the page, placed dots on each side to represent ships, and took turns making a pen flick toward the opposing fleet.
A single dot was a small ship. Two nearby dots made a larger ship, and four dots formed the battleship. If the ink line crossed a dot, the ship was hit. Cross every dot belonging to a ship and it was sunk. The aim was to sink the opposing fleet before your own disappeared under a web of hand-drawn attack lines.
The design rule that survived all the way to release: it still needs to feel like a finger, a pen and a piece of paper—not a conventional tap-to-target Battleship game.
What changed on the way to release
The original prototype grew considerably during testing. The underlying flick mechanic stayed simple, but the surrounding game became much more polished: fleets move and turn like boats, the interface adapts to the current situation, progression is saved locally, AI opponents remain intentionally beatable, and the game now has enough structure to support repeated matches rather than a single novelty round.
One or two playersPlay locally against another person or challenge an offline AI captain.
Tactile flick attacksStarting position, initial direction and flick force determine the shot; there is no steering after launch.
Moving fleetsShips can move inside their own waters and use a visible bow to show the direction of travel.
Different handlingSmall craft can turn quickly while larger ships need more room and change heading gradually.
Campaign progressionPlayers build toward larger fleets, earn credits and retain progress, names and scores on the device.
Adaptive HUDThe latest interface hides unavailable bonuses and can minimise around ships so the play area stays readable.
Recreating the biro flick on a touchscreen
In FlickFleet, the player places a finger on their own half of the paper and flicks toward the opponent. The starting position affects the power of the attack: the farther the finger begins from the centre line, the more force the shot receives.
Once the push begins, the direction is locked from the first instant of movement. The player cannot steer the line after launch. It travels across the paper, and any ship dots it crosses are damaged. That small restriction is what preserves the risk, imperfection and satisfaction of the original pen flick.
Ships that behave like boats
Each ship has a defined front. A small chevron sits ahead of the leading dot to show the bow. Movement follows that heading, so ships travel forward rather than sliding sideways or instantly reversing.
Small craft can turn more sharply. Two-dot ships have a smaller steering limit, and the four-dot battleship changes direction only gradually. A ship may stay anchored during a turn, while another begins moving during an attack. The result is still visually simple—dots, lines and paper—but there is now a genuine positional layer underneath it.
Progression without losing the original game
Learn the flick: early play uses smaller fleets so the attack mechanic is easy to understand.
Earn points and credits: hits, sinks and wins feed progression.
Build the fleet: additional ships and later-game options expand the tactical choices.
Keep progressing: names, progress, credits, fleet choices and high scores are stored locally.
An AI captain that is allowed to miss
The opponent uses lightweight offline game logic rather than a large language model. It evaluates the board and selects a plausible flick, but controlled aiming error prevents the computer from feeling unnaturally perfect. Easier captains make wider mistakes, while higher difficulties become more focused without turning every turn into a guaranteed hit.
Why keep the AI local? A flick is fundamentally a geometry and probability problem. Local logic responds immediately, does not need an internet connection, protects the simple privacy model, and is easier to tune for fair play.
From prototype tests to a released iPhone game
Before the App Store release, the project went through multiple internal iterations. One of the later development milestones was tracked as v4.7.0 build 28, with the adaptive HUD and other refinements in place. The project also accumulated 73 XCTest methods covering important behaviour and regression checks.
Release milestone: Apple completed review of FlickFleet and approved App Store version 1.0 for iOS. The game is now publicly distributed under the name FlickFleet.
The name changed; the idea did not
Paper Fleet Duel remains the development-project name used throughout the design history and on these Know & Guide pages. FlickFleet is the public App Store name. They are the same game and the same experiment: take a tiny pen-and-paper memory and see how far it can be developed without polishing away the thing that made it fun in the first place.
Download, support and privacy
FlickFleet is available from Apple now. The Know & Guide support and privacy pages remain the home for release information, troubleshooting and issue reporting.

resources.description: In the world of AI, failure is often more instructive than success. Project RAGGY (Retrieval-Augmented Generation for General Yield) was our attempt to build a "universal knowledge base" that could instantly answer any question about our internal codebases.
resources.text:
Project RAGGY: Why It Failed
Posted: November 2025 Project Started: September 1, 2025
In the world of AI, failure is often more instructive than success. Project RAGGY (Retrieval-Augmented Generation for General Yield) was our attempt to build a "universal knowledge base" that could instantly answer any question about our internal codebases.
The Ambition
We wanted to solve the context window problem. Instead of feeding an LLM entire files, RAGGY would index every function, class, and comment in a vector database. The goal was to have an AI that "knew" the entire project history without needing to read it all at once.
The Roadblocks
The theory was sound, but the reality was messy. We encountered three fatal flaws:
Stale Data: Code changes fast. Keeping the vector database in sync with the live repo proved to be a computational nightmare. RAGGY was often confident but wrong, citing code that had been deleted days ago.
Context Fragmentation: By chopping code into small chunks for retrieval, RAGGY lost the "big picture." It could explain a single function perfectly but failed to understand how that function fit into the broader architecture.
Cost vs. Value: The cost of embedding and re-embedding code for every commit outweighed the time saved by using the tool.
The Pivot
We shut down RAGGY in late October 2025. But the technology wasn't wasted. We realized that instead of a "universal know-it-all," we needed a "current-context expert." This led to the development of the Context-Aware Monitor in the AI Manager, which focuses only on the active task and relevant files, rather than trying to memorize the entire history.
RAGGY failed so the AI Manager could succeed.

A survivor looking for the truth
Stealing starts with a timed lock
resources.text:
Development journal / First look
Smithers: Karma, crafting and the cost of survival
A young survivor returns to the place where everything was taken from her. Between the sword fights and the search for answers, every stolen treasure and carefully gathered ingredient becomes part of her journey.
September 17, 2026 · Know & Guide · Playable development build
The Buried Archive: a place to trade, craft and uncover the past. In-game development capture, September 13. Select any screenshot to view it at full size.
The storyHow it playsKarmaCraftingStealingThe seven chapters
Smithers is a side-scrolling fantasy action adventure being built in Unity. You guide a hooded fighter through towns, forests, caves, marshes and ruined strongholds. Combat and platforming move the adventure forward; conversations, discoveries, supplies and reputation give those encounters their context.
The interesting decisions often happen between fights. Do you spend gold on training, gather ingredients for the next stretch, or break into a private home? A useful item can solve an immediate problem while leaving Smithers with a worse reputation when she next needs a merchant.
A survivor looking for the truth
Smithers was a child when goblins, led by an Ogre, destroyed her home and killed her family. She survived on the streets before a blind master took her in and trained her. Now she returns to discover why the attack happened and who stood behind it.
That opening gives her skills a history: a street survivor knows how to get through a locked door; a trained fighter knows how to stand her ground. The player decides how she uses both. Her search gradually connects the ruined community to guardians, ancient seals and a struggle over a much greater gate.
The opening story introduces Smithers before the adventure begins. Fresh in-game capture, September 17.
How the adventure works
Explore a chapter, fight its enemies, investigate its story clues and prepare for the major encounter ahead. Sword combat, throwing daggers and smoke bombs sit alongside traversal skills. Character progression runs to level 25; double jump unlocks at character level 3 and hover/glide at level 7.
01 · ExploreFind routes, clues, resources and private dwellings.
02 · PrepareCraft supplies, visit traders and buy training.
03 · ConfrontUse movement and combat to overcome enemies and bosses.
04 · Carry forwardKeep earned progression and face the next chapter.
Easy, Normal and Hell offer increasingly demanding encounters. Replaying chapters retains earned levels, gold, inventory and purchased sword training. Previously claimed discoveries and stolen valuables remain claimed, so replaying does not turn the same chest into an endless reward.
Karma: your choices follow you
Karma runs from −100 to +100, with zero as neutral. Positive Karma appears green; negative Karma appears red. Gathering natural materials has no Karma cost. Stealing a valuable costs 8 Karma. Helpful actions, including lighting lamps and some survivor story interactions, can build it back up.
−100Negative Karma
0Neutral
+100Positive Karma
Reputation changes the economy. Positive Karma gradually discounts shop prices, reaching 25% off at +100. Negative Karma raises prices, and merchants refuse to trade at −50 or below.
A concrete example: from neutral, one theft takes Smithers to −8 Karma. A purchase with a base price of 100 gold now costs 108. Seven thefts without any positive changes take her to −56, beyond the trading cutoff. The treasure has a cost beyond the lock pick.
The system also ties Smithers to the town around her: damage to its buildings can reduce Karma. Death removes positive Karma while leaving negative Karma in place. It does not erase the consequences of theft.
The red theft notification makes the consequence explicit: a valuable gained, eight Karma lost. September 17 development capture; the message remains visible as the capture sequence moves to the jungle hut.
Crafting: turn exploration into supplies
Sticks, vine fibre, pine cones, flowers, cave mushrooms and well water all have a purpose. Press F near a resource to gather it, C beside a crafting table to open recipes, and I to inspect your traveller's bag. Use the Supplies & equipment tab to consume healing items or refill ammunition.
Most gathered resources stay depleted across scene changes; wells refill. Ingredients and finished supplies travel with you between chapters and saved sessions. These are the five recipes in the current build:
3 throwing daggers
3 sticks + 2 vine fibre
Transfer from your bag to refill your dagger ammunition.
Healing potion
2 red blossoms + 1 water + 1 cave mushroom
Restores 40% of maximum health.
Bandage
2 white yarrow + 1 vine fibre
Restores 20% of maximum health.
Smoke bomb
2 pine cones + 1 cave mushroom + 1 vine fibre
Refills the smoke-bomb ability from your bag.
Marsh tonic
2 violet blooms + 1 white yarrow + 1 water
Clears a current slowing effect. New swamp exposure can slow you again.
A cave mushroom could become healing or a smoke bomb. Vine fibre is shared by several recipes. That creates a small preparation puzzle: make what solves the next problem, while keeping enough material for the route beyond it.
The actual crafting interface shows what each recipe needs and what it does. This September 17 capture uses an empty bag, so the buttons correctly say “Need ingredients.”
Stealing starts with a timed lock
Private homes and jungle huts offer a different kind of challenge. Buy lock picks at a shop, approach a locked entrance and press ↑. The current lock-picking game asks you to set individual pins and finish turning the lock before their timers expire.
Insert the pick. Hold Space to begin.
Choose and lift a pin. Use A/D or the left/right arrows, then hold Space.
Release on the gold line. A correctly set pin starts its own countdown.
Set the remaining pins and turn. Hold Space to finish opening the lock before a set pin drops.
Too much force can break a pick. A timed-out pin drops without consuming one, but interrupts the turn. Chapter 1 locks have two pins; Chapter 2 locks have three. Later automatic locks become more complex. Press Esc to cancel safely.
Once inside, press T near a valuable to steal it, or leave it alone and exit with ↑. Unlocking a door and taking someone's property are separate actions. The Karma penalty is applied when the valuable is taken.
Current build detail: stolen goods are recorded in the bag with a stated value. They do not automatically become spendable gold, and selling stolen goods is not implemented yet.
One pin set, one still to go. The green pin's countdown turns a lock into a timing puzzle. Fresh in-game capture, September 17.
Beyond the lock is a separate interior with a valuable to take—or leave behind. Fresh in-game capture, September 17.
One journey, seven chapters
The campaign expands from a personal search into a story about power and responsibility. Its current playable route moves through seven chapters:
Town, forest and cave. Return to the community, prepare in town and descend toward the Ogre encounter.
The dark forest and jungle. Follow the trail through a new landscape, with private huts, a market and the serpent encounter.
The Drowned Marsh. Cross dangerous wetlands, investigate the First Seal and confront Varkesh.
The Buried Archive. Search the records for the truth about Smithers' family and face the Bound Keeper.
The Broken Mountain. Climb toward an occupied sanctuary and the Black-Crystal Envoy.
The Black Citadel. Push through prison approaches and furnace yards toward the Regent of Ash.
Return to the First Gate. Come back to the ruined home ground for the final confrontation.
Discoveries and conversations matter as well as combat. Later boss encounters require the chapter's discoveries before the confrontation can proceed. Smithers needs to understand what happened as she becomes strong enough to act on it.
Story spoilers: the guardians, the gate and Karma's ending
The archive reveals that Smithers' family and her blind trainer were guardians. The mountain exposes a stolen counterseal and crystal coercion; the citadel reveals the Regent's funding of the campaign to control the greater gate. Those revelations do not excuse Varkesh's responsibility for ordering the massacre.
Smithers returns home to close the gate, choosing guardianship over domination. The current ending text changes with Karma: at +5 or higher, it includes rebuilding and community; below that, redemption begins in greater isolation.
The Broken Mountain makes story discovery part of the encounter: recover the relic and learn the truth before confronting the Envoy. Development capture, September 13.
Where Smithers stands today
This is a look at a playable game in development, not a public launch announcement. The seven-chapter route and the systems described here are implemented in the current Unity project. The later chapters are a first playable pass, with further work still needed on art, encounter balance and presentation. Some survivor rescues are currently dialogue interactions rather than escort missions.
The screenshots come from the running game during development checks. Fresh captures of the origin story, crafting, lock-picking and hut sequence were taken on September 17; the two later-chapter views were captured on September 13. Values and presentation may change as the game develops.
What ties the adventure together is the relationship between its systems. Exploring gives Smithers supplies and answers. Crafting gives her ways to survive. Stealing tests what she is prepared to take from others. Karma carries those choices into the next shop—and eventually into the way her story closes.

resources.description: The development story behind Starfall Interceptor, a 30-level iPhone and iPad space arcade game where the goal is to liberate mind-controlled pilots rather than destroy them.
headings: Starfall Interceptor: Turning a Classic Space-Shooter Idea into a Game About Liberation
What made it into the released game
resources.text:
App Store launch Starfall
Interceptor You are not here to destroy them. You are here to set them free.
Starfall Interceptor: Turning a Classic Space-Shooter Idea into a Game About Liberation
Released: August 25, 2026 • Category: iOS Game Development
StarfallInterceptor version 1.0 is now available on the Apple App Store.
The finished release supports iPhone and iPad and takes the player through a thirty-level campaign across three worlds.
Download StarfallInterceptor
Starfall Interceptor started with a familiar arcade question: what would a modern iPhone game inspired by the speed and pressure of classic horizontal shooters feel like? The interesting part came when the usual premise was turned around.
Instead of assuming every alien ship should be destroyed, Starfall asks the player to discover what is really happening. The pilots attacking the planet are being controlled by an ancient force called The Veil. The player's primary weapon, the SoulHeal laser, is therefore a liberation tool. Hit a controlled ship enough times and the pilot is released from the Veil's influence, the craft changes into a bright liberation state, and it leaves the battle rather than exploding as another enemy kill.
The central design decision changed the whole game.
Once the goal became liberation rather than destruction, score, sound, animation, enemy behaviour, boss design and even the story all had to support that idea. Liberated pilots acknowledge the player, while civilians and buildings below the battle become people and places worth protecting rather than background decoration.
What made it into the released game
SoulHeal combatEnemy ships can be freed from the Veil instead of simply destroyed.
Three worlds, thirty levelsThe campaign grows from the opening planet into new fleets, colour families and escalating formations.
Mothership battlesMajor encounters use large multi-part structures with changing vulnerabilities and attack patterns.
HyperdriveA powerful temporary burst gives the player a way to escape pressure and reposition during difficult battles.
Persistent upgradesStar Credits improve shields, regeneration, weapons, thrust and Hyperdrive cooling over the pilot's career.
Beginner, Normal and ExpertThe same campaign can be replayed with different speed and aggression profiles.
Civilians and buildingsProtecting the ground matters. The battle is happening over a living world, not an empty scrolling backdrop.
Swappable controlsJoystick and FIRE/HYPER positions can be reversed for left- or right-handed players.
Dynamic audioCalm and battle music, lasers, impacts, Hyperdrive and liberated-pilot voices help communicate the state of the fight.
How the campaign grew
Build the feel first. The early work concentrated on joystick movement, the centred player ship, continuous world scrolling and a laser that felt immediate.
Give the enemies purpose. The Veil story turned ordinary targets into controlled pilots and created the SoulHeal liberation mechanic.
Make the world matter. Civilians, buildings, missiles and ground attacks gave the player reasons to defend rather than simply chase a high score.
Add progression. Shields, Star Credits, upgrades, achievements, ranks and saved career progress gave each run a longer-term purpose.
Expand the universe. New planets, ship families and two very different mothership designs pushed the game toward its thirty-level structure.
Finish the current frontier. Level 30 closes this campaign with the promise that more worlds remain to be liberated and that the Veil has not been completely removed.
A game built through iteration
Starfall changed repeatedly during development. Camera scale, joystick sensitivity, the amount of world movement, boss size, projectile damage, tutorial behaviour, level pacing, ship art, audio, screen layout and difficulty all went through multiple passes. The goal was not to preserve the first version of the idea; it was to preserve the feeling that made the idea worth building.
The release also reflects a practical mobile-game philosophy: play should work offline, progress should live locally, controls should remain understandable, and the player should be able to pick up the game for a quick session without creating an account.
Where Starfall goes next
Version 1.0 completes the first three-world campaign, but the ending deliberately leaves room for more. The Veil is larger than the worlds already visited, and the existing progression system allows the player to carry score and persistent abilities into another run at a different difficulty.
For now, the important milestone is simpler: Starfall Interceptor has moved from prototype, to repeated Xcode testing, to App Store submission, and finally to a released iPhone and iPad game.

resources.text:
Studio AI: The Great Transfer
Posted: November 2025 Project Started: August 15, 2025
Studio AI was conceived as the ultimate "Idea-to-Reality" engine. The premise was simple yet ambitious: a unified interface where a user could describe a software application in natural language, and Studio AI would orchestrate a swarm of agents to build, test, and deploy it in real-time.
The Vision
We built the prototype using a multi-agent architecture. One agent handled the frontend design (using a custom component library), another managed the backend schema (generating SQL and API endpoints), and a third acted as the "Product Manager," ensuring the user's requirements were met.
For three months, we pushed the boundaries of what autonomous coding agents could do. We successfully generated simple CRUD apps and landing pages with zero human intervention.
The Transfer
However, as the project grew, we realized that the infrastructure required to scale Studio AI was massive. It wasn't just a "project" anymore; it was becoming a platform that needed its own dedicated ecosystem.
In November 2025, we made the strategic decision to transfer the core technology of Studio AI to a larger entity better equipped to handle the computational load and security requirements. This wasn't an end, but a graduation. The DNA of Studio AI—specifically its "Manager" agent logic—was extracted and refined to create the Unified Project Agent (UPA) that powers this very website today.
Legacy
Studio AI taught us that while AI can write code, the true value lies in architecting the system. That lesson is the foundation of our new mission: turning coders into architects.

resources.text:
Private native iPhone prototype Surya Shakti
Voice Coach
Building a Voice-Guided Surya Shakti Practice Companion
Posted: July 19, 2026 • Category: Yoga Technology
I have been developing a private, native iPhone application to support my daily Surya Shakti practice. The purpose is simple: let the phone announce each movement in English and then Sanskrit, wait for me to repeat the Sanskrit name, and only then continue to the next movement.
The application is designed as a personal practice companion for someone who has already learned the process correctly. It is not intended to teach Surya Shakti, replace a qualified teacher, alter the practice, or provide independent yoga instruction.
How the prototype works
English, then SanskritEach movement is spoken first in English and then by its Sanskrit name.
Listen and waitA short beep signals that the microphone is ready, and the app waits for the Sanskrit response.
Gentle correctionTwo beeps request another attempt. After two missed attempts, the Sanskrit name is spoken again before listening resumes.
AirPods supportThe microphone, spoken guidance, voice test, and playback test can use compatible AirPods or the iPhone.
Practice trackingThe app records completed cycles, practice days, current streak, longest streak, and lifetime totals on the device.
Pronunciation reflectionAt the end of a session, optional AI feedback summarises which Sanskrit names may need more practice.
Why I built it
During practice, I wanted a simple hands-free rhythm: hear the movement, move into the posture, repeat the Sanskrit name, and continue without touching the screen. The application keeps the established 18-position sequence unchanged while helping me remember the names and observe my consistency over time.
The current build is a standalone SwiftUI iPhone application rather than a website. It runs from its own app icon, stores practice records locally, supports a manual “I said it” control when speech recognition struggles, and can use optional cloud voice and transcription services for improved recognition.
Current status: This is a private personal prototype. It is not an official Isha Foundation application, it is not endorsed by Isha Foundation, and it is not currently available for public download.
Approval before any public release
Before making the application available to other people, I intend to seek written approval from Isha Foundation. Only if that approval is granted would I consider offering the iPhone application free of charge.
I would also follow any guidance provided about naming, presentation, pronunciation, teaching boundaries, intellectual property, privacy, safety, and whether an application of this kind should be released at all.
Official reference: Learn more from Isha Foundation’s article, Classical Yoga: Surya Kriya and Surya Shakti.
Respecting the practice
The technology is intended to support memory and pronunciation, not to reinterpret the practice. Anyone interested in learning Surya Shakti should use official Isha Foundation information and receive appropriate instruction rather than relying on an app or an online sequence guide.
I will continue testing the private version on my own iPhone, particularly the AirPods microphone route, Sanskrit speech recognition, spoken prompts, repetition logic, cycle counting, and end-of-session feedback.

resources.title: The Cortex Manifesto | Cortex OS
resources.description: Paper 1 of the Cortex OS research programme: a manifesto for AI-native computing.
resources.text:
Cortex OS · Paper 1
The Cortex Manifesto
Towards AI-native computing: a research proposal for systems organised around intelligence and human intent.
CORTEX-WP-001Version 1.0.0-draftResearch ProposalJuly 2026
← Return to Cortex OS
Abstract
Computing has reached an architectural transition point. For more than seventy years, computer systems have been designed around deterministic execution: hardware executes instructions, operating systems allocate resources, applications perform specialised tasks, and humans coordinate those applications through graphical interfaces.
Artificial intelligence has emerged as a new computational paradigm, yet most systems continue to treat AI as another application inside an operating system that was never designed for adaptive reasoning. This paper proposes a different premise: instead of adapting AI to existing operating systems, future computing systems should be designed around intelligence itself.
We call this paradigm AI-native computing. Cortex OS is not presented as a finished operating system, but as a research programme exploring architectures in which reasoning becomes a first-class system capability while deterministic control remains foundational.
1. Historical context
Every major shift in computing has changed the primary abstraction presented to people. Early computers exposed hardware directly. Operating systems abstracted hardware. Graphical interfaces abstracted operating systems. The Internet abstracted individual computers. Cloud computing abstracted infrastructure.
Artificial intelligence may now abstract software itself. Current operating systems assume that people launch applications to perform tasks. Increasingly, people express intentions rather than application-specific commands. The existing software stack reflects assumptions that no longer align with this emerging mode of interaction.
2. The central hypothesis
Intelligence should become the organising principle of future computing systems rather than another software application.
This hypothesis does not imply removing deterministic software. It proposes reorganising system architecture around adaptive reasoning while preserving deterministic execution wherever correctness, safety and reproducibility are essential.
3. Intelligence is not an application
Current AI systems typically exist as applications. The operating system remains unaware of goals, context, priorities and intent. As a result, AI systems repeatedly reconstruct information that already exists elsewhere in the device.
Cortex OS proposes that intelligence participate directly in system coordination. Rather than asking which application should perform a task, the system should first ask what objective the user is trying to achieve. Applications become implementation details. Intent becomes the primary computational object.
4. From applications to cognitive services
Traditional operating systems organise software into independent applications. Cortex OS proposes a set of specialised cognitive services, including communication, memory, planning, security, environmental awareness, learning and system management.
Each service maintains expertise within its own domain while cooperating through structured interfaces. No individual service is assumed to possess complete knowledge. Collective reasoning emerges through coordination.
5. Distributed cognition
Biological nervous systems distribute intelligence. Reflexes occur without conscious thought. Motor control operates independently from language. Memory is distributed across specialised structures. Human cognition scales because autonomy exists at multiple levels simultaneously.
Cortex OS adopts this principle. Specialist cognitive components operate semi-independently while remaining coordinated through higher-level executive reasoning. Higher layers define intent; lower layers execute domain-specific behaviour locally.
6. Determinism and adaptation
Adaptive systems introduce uncertainty. Operating systems require predictability. These objectives should not be treated as mutually exclusive.
Deterministic components remain responsible for scheduling, memory protection, hardware isolation, security boundaries, resource allocation and physical device control. Adaptive components remain responsible for planning, interpretation, optimisation, personalisation and goal management.
The AI may decide what should happen. Trusted deterministic services decide whether and how that action may safely occur.
7. Human-centred computing
Future computing should minimise cognitive friction. People increasingly describe intentions rather than software procedures. A request such as “prepare tomorrow's presentation” should not require the user to manually coordinate files, calendars, research tools, design software and communications.
An AI-native system interprets the objective, coordinates available resources, asks for clarification where necessary, and explains consequential decisions. The computer evolves from a tool requiring constant supervision into a collaborative reasoning system.
8. Hardware must evolve
Software architecture cannot fully realise AI-native computing without corresponding hardware evolution. Future devices may contain specialised processors for language, perception, memory, planning, security and sensor integration.
These processors could cooperate through high-bandwidth interconnects and shared memory while preserving deterministic system control. This remains a research hypothesis requiring simulation, prototyping and measurement.
9. Research principles
Reasoning should exist as close as practical to the problem it solves.
Deterministic behaviour must remain verifiable.
Learning should be observable, auditable and reversible.
Privacy should default to local computation whenever feasible.
Specialisation should replace unnecessary generalisation.
Human intent should become the primary interface.
Hardware and software should be designed together rather than independently.
Every architectural claim should be testable through implementation.
10. Research methodology
Cortex OS is an iterative research programme rather than a fixed specification. Every significant architectural proposal should progress through conceptual formulation, technical specification, prototype implementation and experimental evaluation.
Claims unsupported by experimentation remain hypotheses rather than conclusions. Project documents should explicitly classify material as established engineering, inspired design, hypothesis, experimental result, prototype behaviour or future vision.
11. Limitations
This manifesto does not claim that current operating systems should be replaced immediately, nor that probabilistic AI can safely perform every operating-system function. Trust, verification, scheduling, energy efficiency, hardware support and safe adaptation remain open research problems.
A practical first prototype may use an existing Linux kernel and unlockable Android hardware. This does not define the final architecture; it provides a measurable platform for testing cognitive services before attempting custom hardware or a new kernel.
12. Call for collaboration
The transition to AI-native computing cannot be achieved by advances in language models alone. It requires collaboration among operating-system researchers, AI scientists, hardware architects, embedded-systems engineers, security specialists, interaction designers and ethicists.
Cortex OS provides a common architectural language through which ideas may be evaluated, challenged, implemented, improved or rejected.
Conclusion
Computing has always advanced by changing its organising abstractions. The next abstraction may not be the application, the file or even the operating system. It may be intent.
Cortex OS proposes that intelligence become a native property of computing rather than an optional feature layered onto existing architectures. Whether that vision proves correct is less important than investigating it rigorously.
The purpose of this manifesto is not to declare the future. It is to begin building it.
