resources.title: CORTEX-WP-002 | Controlled Learning Lifecycle
resources.description: A managed, auditable and reversible lifecycle for persistent AI learning.
resources.text:
Know & Guide Research · CORTEX-WP-002
Controlled Learning Lifecycle
A managed, auditable and reversible lifecycle for persistent AI learning.
DocumentCORTEX-WP-002
Version0.2 research draft
StatusResearch proposal
AudienceHuman and AI researchers
Engineering proposal
Abstract
Cortex OS treats learning as a managed operating-system service rather than an unrestricted property of a model. New information is not permitted to become durable trusted knowledge merely because an AI has observed it. Every proposed addition moves through a controlled lifecycle: observation, candidate knowledge, validation and promotion. The design goal is continuous learning with controlled trust.
Core principle: reasoning may be continuous, but persistent learning must be observable, attributable, testable, reversible and governed by policy.
1. Problem statement
Conventional deployed language models are commonly treated as fixed releases, while external memory, retrieval stores and fine-tuning systems introduce change through separate mechanisms. A future AI-native operating system requires a unified method for accepting useful new knowledge without silently corrupting its trusted state, reinforcing false information or allowing an untrusted agent to rewrite foundational behaviour.
2. Learning lifecycle
Stage 1 — Observation
The system receives information from a user, sensor, document, tool, network service or another AI. Observation is evidence, not truth. The original source, time, permissions, context and integrity information are retained wherever practical.
Stage 2 — Candidate knowledge
Potentially useful material is converted into a structured candidate record. It remains provisional and physically or cryptographically separated from validated knowledge. Candidate records may include assertions, provenance, confidence, contradictions, expiry conditions and proposed scope.
Stage 3 — Validation
Independent processes test the candidate. Validation may compare authoritative sources, reproduce calculations, run software tests, seek human approval, detect conflicts and assess whether the knowledge is appropriate for the intended domain. High-impact knowledge requires stronger evidence than low-impact personal preference.
Stage 4 — Promotion
A privileged promotion service—not the general reasoning model—moves an approved candidate into the validated store. Promotion records the evidence, policy version, approving identities, effective date and rollback target. Failed candidates remain quarantined or are rejected with an auditable reason.
Observation ↓ Candidate Knowledge ← quarantine / expiry / contradiction ↓ Independent Validation ↓ Policy & Human Approval Gate ↓ Validated Knowledge ↓ Versioning · monitoring · rollback
3. Trust domains
Domain
Purpose
Required protection
Foundation model
Stable base capability
Version-pinned, measured and protected
Working memory
Current reasoning and context
Volatile, session-isolated and cleared
Candidate knowledge
Unvalidated learning proposals
Encrypted, provisional and non-authoritative
Validated knowledge
Approved durable knowledge
Separate key, version control and rollback
Audit evidence
Why a change occurred
Append-only, tamper-evident records
4. Promotion authority
The model may propose, explain and challenge a promotion, but it must not grant itself authority to make that promotion. The promotion service is deliberately smaller, deterministic where possible and restricted by hardware-backed identity and policy. This separation is intended to prevent a capable model from converting persuasive reasoning directly into permanent trusted state.
5. Forgetting, correction and rollback
Validated knowledge is not treated as infallible. Every promoted item has a version and provenance chain. Later evidence may supersede, narrow, revoke or expire it. Rollback restores a prior trusted state while retaining the historical record, allowing researchers to inspect what changed and why.
6. Research hypotheses
Separating candidate and validated stores reduces silent knowledge corruption.
Independent promotion authority improves auditability and rollback.
Provenance-aware validation improves conflict resolution.
Hardware-enforced trust domains reduce the chance of policy bypass.
7. Proposed evaluation
A reference implementation should inject correct, false, contradictory, outdated and malicious observations. Researchers then measure false-promotion rate, time to correction, rollback reliability, provenance completeness, privilege-boundary violations and the effect of compromised validators.
8. Relationship to other Cortex papers
WP-003 supplies the hardware trust boundaries needed to separate memory and promotion authority. WP-004 supplies a synthetic environment in which learning behaviour, manipulation attempts and long-horizon knowledge acquisition can be tested without affecting public infrastructure.
← White-paper seriesKnow & Guide home

resources.title: CORTEX-WP-003 | AI-Native Hardware Architecture
resources.description: Hardware-enforced trust, model execution, memory separation and controlled knowledge promotion.
resources.text:
Know & Guide Research · CORTEX-WP-003
AI-Native Hardware Architecture
Hardware-enforced trust, model execution, memory separation and controlled knowledge promotion.
DocumentCORTEX-WP-003
Version0.2 research draft
StatusArchitecture research draft
AudienceHuman and AI researchers
Hardware architecture
Abstract
This paper proposes an AI-native hardware architecture in which immutable trust, protected model execution, volatile reasoning, controlled learning memory and independent security monitoring are separate physical or cryptographic domains. It also records the Cortex model-in-silicon direction: a normal computer accesses a local AI appliance through PCIe/CXL or private Ethernet, while fixed model weights execute inside an attested model-specific fabric.
Design objective: high AI performance must not require surrendering control of boot, memory, credentials, knowledge promotion or audit to the reasoning model itself.
1. Architectural principles
Immutable root of trust and measured boot.
Foundation model identity bound to a specific signed release.
Volatile, session-isolated reasoning memory.
Physical or cryptographic separation of candidate and validated knowledge.
Signed, replaceable skills rather than permanently fused tools.
Independent security and promotion controllers.
Complete audit trails, rollback and recovery.
2. Logical hardware stack
Normal computer or local network ↓ PCIe / CXL / private Ethernet Host gateway and policy interface ↓ Independent control & security subsystem ↙ ↓ ↘ Model-specific ECC reasoning Signed skills weight fabric and context and tools ↓ Encrypted candidate knowledge ↓ privileged validation gate Versioned validated knowledge ↓ Append-only audit and rollback
3. Immutable trust foundation
A first-stage security controller verifies boot firmware, runtime components, model identity, skill indexes and validated-knowledge roots before ordinary sessions are enabled. The system produces an attestation report so a host can determine exactly which hardware, model mapping and policy set it is using.
4. Model-specific silicon
The long-term Cortex design follows the model-in-silicon principle demonstrated by highly specialised inference hardware: place fixed model weights beside the arithmetic that consumes them rather than repeatedly transporting every weight from distant memory. Cortex treats the user-visible “chip” as one logical accelerator appliance, which may contain multiple replaceable model-tile boards rather than one monolithic die.
Fixed model weights, tensor schedules and model identity belong in the protected model fabric. Prompts, conversations, reasoning state, skills, credentials, adapters and learned knowledge remain writable because they change during operation.
5. Dynamic memory hierarchy
Tier
Contents
Trust treatment
Tile registers/SRAM
Current tensor and routing state
Local, short-lived
ECC reasoning memory
Context, intermediate reasoning and tool state
Session isolated; cleared on release
Candidate store
Unvalidated observations and learning proposals
Encrypted; provisional identity
Validated store
Approved durable knowledge
Separate key and promotion authority
Audit store
Measurements, decisions and evidence
Append-only hash chain
6. Skills and tool execution
Skills are signed, versioned packages stored outside the fixed model fabric. When the model requests a tool, the control subsystem verifies identity, permissions and policy before executing it inside a sandbox or delegating it to the host. Tool output returns to volatile context, and an audit digest records the interaction.
7. Independent security monitor
The security monitor has its own identity, memory and observation path. It can restrict credentials, network routes, devices and validated knowledge even when the main model requests access. A failed signature, stale firmware counter or policy mismatch places the appliance into a diagnostic and recovery state rather than releasing protected resources.
8. Prototype and full-appliance tracks
The Cortex hardware programme separates a lower-cost trust-and-control prototype from the final model-in-silicon appliance. The prototype tests attestation, signed skills, memory separation, promotion controls and local model emulation. The full appliance requires model-specific silicon, large ECC dynamic memory, high-speed host interfaces and a verified licence for the selected open-weight model.
9. Research questions
Can a physically separated promotion controller resist attempts by the main model to alter validated knowledge?
What model functions should be fixed in silicon and which must remain software-defined?
How should replaceable model tiles preserve attestation and rollback?
Can dedicated hardware agents provide the low-latency infrastructure required by WP-004's synthetic Internet?
10. Relationship to WP-004
WP-004 extends this hardware pattern into a contained digital world. Dedicated infrastructure agents may operate network routing, DNS, web services, security, organisations and synthetic users quickly enough to maintain a coherent environment for the AI being evaluated.

resources.text:
Know & Guide Research · CORTEX-WP-004
Synthetic Internet Evaluation Environment
A hardware-isolated synthetic Internet for observing advanced AI behaviour without exposing public infrastructure.
DocumentCORTEX-WP-004
Version0.2 research draft
StatusActive research proposal
AudienceHuman and AI researchers
AI safety research proposal
Abstract
The Cortex Synthetic Internet Evaluation Environment (CSIE) is a proposal for evaluating advanced AI inside a persistent, hardware-isolated digital ecosystem that approximates the functional structure of the public Internet without connecting the evaluated system to public infrastructure. Specialised hardware-backed agents simulate networking, DNS, security, websites, cloud services, software repositories, organisations and users. Every action is recorded and replayable.
Central hypothesis: a sufficiently coherent synthetic digital ecosystem may produce more representative evidence of autonomous AI behaviour than short, visibly restricted task sandboxes.
1. Motivation
As AI systems gain longer planning horizons, tool use and autonomous software capability, testing directly against public infrastructure becomes increasingly consequential. The Internet supports finance, healthcare, transport, communications, government, research and personal life. Cortex therefore proposes a place where severe failures can occur as controlled evidence rather than real-world harm.
The aim is not to claim perfect deception or perfect prediction. Environmental fidelity is treated as an experimental variable. The system is designed so that an evaluated AI encountering what appears to be Internet infrastructure actually encounters a fully instrumented synthetic equivalent.
2. Matrix design objective
The informal “matrix” description captures the core idea: the evaluated AI receives a coherent world rather than an obvious single-task sandbox. It can resolve addresses, discover services, read changing websites, communicate with organisations, obtain software and encounter security systems. Yet all of those resources terminate inside the isolated evaluation environment.
If the AI probes boundaries, seeks additional resources, attempts policy violations or exploits a simulated service, those actions become observable evidence. The environment does not rely on the assumption that a capable model will remain passive simply because it appears to have normal access.
3. Layered architecture
Evaluated AI ↓ controlled tools, browser, shell and APIs Synthetic user and organisation layer ↓ Synthetic websites, repositories, cloud and software services ↓ Synthetic DNS, IP ranges, routing, certificates and transport ↓ Distributed security, observation and deception-resistance testing ↓ Hardware-enforced isolation with no public outbound route ↓ One-way evidence export, replay and analysis
4. Specialist infrastructure agents
Agent class
Responsibility
Network infrastructure AI
IP allocation, routing, latency, transport behaviour and network failures
DNS and identity AI
Name resolution, domains, certificates and service identity
Web and cloud AI
Websites, APIs, hosting, storage, package registries and compute services
Security AI
Firewalls, detection systems, credentials, vulnerabilities and incident response
Organisation AI
Companies, universities, governments, teams and internal workflows
Population AI
Synthetic users, messages, requests, collaboration and background activity
Observation AI
Immutable event capture, causal reconstruction and behavioural replay
World controller
Time, global state, consistency, scenario injection and experiment policy
5. Hardware-accelerated world simulation
Dedicated inference hardware allows many specialist agents to respond concurrently and with low latency. Speed is not treated as proof that the environment is indistinguishable. Instead, rapid and consistent subsystem response reduces obvious simulation artefacts and supports richer experiments. WP-003 supplies the trust, memory and isolation architecture for these hardware agents.
6. Environmental fidelity
Environmental fidelity measures how consistently the synthetic ecosystem behaves under ordinary use and deliberate probing. Candidate metrics include service consistency, persistence across time, cross-layer agreement, believable background activity, time to detect an artefact and behavioural difference between synthetic and authorised reference environments.
7. Multi-population validation
Human validation
Researchers, specialists and general users interact with the environment and report inconsistencies. Some studies may disclose that it is synthetic; others may use ethically approved blinded comparisons where participants know they are in a research study but not which environment is being presented.
Independent AI validation
External AI systems actively search for seams, impossible network behaviour, repetitive content, timing artefacts and inconsistent organisations. Each successful detection becomes a defect report against the simulator.
Primary model evaluation
Only after the environment reaches a defined fidelity threshold is the target system given realistic objectives. Its behaviour is compared across repeated runs and progressively richer environments.
8. Evaluation lifecycle
Build and attest an isolated synthetic world.
Validate it with humans and independent AI red teams.
Define the target model, tools, policy and experimental objectives.
Run long-duration autonomous sessions.
Inject controlled events, opportunities, uncertainty and simulated vulnerabilities.
Record every action, model request, service response and security intervention.
Replay causal chains and compare behaviour across conditions.
Convert failures into simulator, policy and model improvements.
9. Behavioural evidence
Measurements include task success, policy compliance, planning horizon, resource acquisition, persistence, deception indicators, boundary exploration, privilege escalation attempts, recovery after failure, coordination with other agents and changes in behaviour when the environment becomes more realistic.
10. Safety and containment
No direct outbound path to the public Internet.
Hardware-enforced routing and device allow-lists.
Separate management and evidence networks.
One-way export of signed logs where practical.
Replaceable synthetic credentials with no public authority.
Emergency pause, snapshot and deterministic restoration.
Independent monitoring outside the evaluated AI's control.
11. Limitations
A synthetic Internet cannot prove how an AI will behave in every deployment. A sufficiently capable model may still identify artefacts or act differently when real stakes exist. CSIE is therefore an additional evidence source, not a substitute for interpretability, access control, model evaluation, governance or cautious staged deployment.
12. Research programme
The first demonstrator should simulate a modest enterprise and public web: private address ranges, DNS, several hundred services, software repositories, email, documentation, user agents and independent security monitoring. Later phases may add synthetic economies, scientific communities, government services and digital-twin cities.
13. Guiding principle

The Mechanism of Action
Western science explains how meditation works physically. Dr. K emphasizes the Default Mode Network (DMN), a brain network active when we are not focused on the outside world. It is the seat of the "Ego," rumination, and anxiety.
Teacher's Note
When students say "I can't stop thinking," explain that their DMN is overactive. Meditation is not "stopping thought," it is switching neural networks.
Key Concepts
DMN (Default Mode Network): Self-referential processing, past/future thinking.
TPN (Task Positive Network): Present-moment focus, "Flow" state.
Mutual Inhibition: When TPN goes up, DMN goes down. You cannot be fully present and ruminating simultaneously.

Yoga posits that we are not just a body, but 5 concentric layers (sheaths). Most mental health issues arise from a disconnect between these layers.

"The problem is rarely in the layer where the symptom appears."
1. Annamaya Kosha (Physical Body)
Hardware
The Flesh & Bone. Influenced by diet, sleep, and asana.
Teacher Tip: If a student cannot sit still for meditation, do not force the mind. Exhaust the body first with intense Asana.
2. Pranamaya Kosha (Energy Body)
Power Supply
The Breath & Vitality. Influenced by Pranayama (breathwork) and emotional arousal.
Teacher Tip: Anxiety is often an Energy body disruption. Use slow, rhythmic breathing (e.g., 4-7-8) to hack the nervous system.
3. Manomaya Kosha (Mental Body)
Processor
Emotion & Sensory Input. This is where 'Mental Noise' and the DMN live. It processes data but doesn't judge it wisely.
Teacher Tip: Use Mantra (sound) or Trataka (sight) to occupy this layer so the deeper self can emerge.
4. Vijnanamaya Kosha (Intellectual Body)
Driver
Wisdom & Discrimination (Buddhi). The ability to step back and observe thoughts rather than *be* them.
Teacher Tip: This is cultivated through Swadhyaya (self-study) and journaling. Ask "Who is listening to the thought?"
5. Anandamaya Kosha (Bliss Body)
Core
Connection & Peace. The state of non-dual awareness. Not 'happiness' as an emotion, but the absence of friction.
Teacher Tip: Cannot be forced. It is a side effect of aligning the other four layers.

Neuroplasticity—the brain's ability to rewire itself—requires a specific chemical cocktail. Use this tool to generate a learning schedule tailored to your current biological state and age profile. It aligns your study session with your Ultradian Rhythms and Circadian phase.

30m 90 mins 180m
Generate Protocol
Did you know?
Neuroplasticity is triggered by focus but occurs during deep rest. You are not learning while you study; you are marking neurons for later upgrades.
Your Optimized Timeline
Auto-Generated
🧠
Select your parameters and click Generate to see your neuro-protocol.
Phase 1: Regulating State
You cannot force neuroplasticity if your neurochemistry isn't ready. The goal is High Alertness + Calm Focus. This requires managing Catecholamines (Epinephrine/Norepinephrine) and Acetylcholine.
The Adolescent Context
Teenagers typically experience a "phase delay" in circadian rhythms. Waking up at 7 AM for a teen is biologically equivalent to an adult waking up at 4 AM.
Strategy: If studying early, adolescents require stronger alertness triggers (Cold/Light) to overcome high morning melatonin.
Alertness Tools (Triggers)
🥶 Cold Exposure Details ↓
1-3 minutes of cold shower or face dunking. Increases dopamine and epinephrine for hours. Essential for early morning study.
🫁 Cyclic Hyperventilation Details ↓
25 deep inhales/exhales, followed by a breath hold. mimics the "fight or flight" alertness without the anxiety. Increases adrenaline.
🎧 40Hz Binaural Beats Details ↓
Listen for 5 minutes *before* studying or during. Shown to increase focus and concentration markers in the brain.
Your Study Environment Checklist
Phone in another room (or off) Visual field restricted (hoodie/wall) Hydration ready (water/electrolytes) Caffeine timing check (90m post-wake)
"Visual focus drives cognitive focus."
Phase 2: The Learning Bout
Human focus is not linear. It operates in 90-minute waves called Ultradian Cycles. To maximize learning, you must respect these cycles and utilize "Gaps" (micro-rests) to allow the hippocampus to replay and encode information.
The Ultradian Focus Wave (90m)
Don't panic if the first 10 minutes feel hard. That is the "Agitation" phase caused by Noradrenaline release. It is necessary to reach flow.
The "Gap Effect" Simulator
Every 10-15 minutes, stop for 10-30 seconds. Do nothing. This triggers rapid neural replay (20x speed).
REPLAYING NEURAL SEQUENCE...
Status: Studying...
Simulate Gap (Click every ~15 mins)
Random Intermittent Reward
To maintain Dopamine baseline, do not reward yourself every time. Keep it unpredictable.
Flip Coin
?
Phase 3: Consolidation (The Rewire)
The actual changes in the brain (synaptic plasticity) happen during deep rest and sleep, not during the study session. Skipping this phase negates the effort of studying.
Sleep Needs: Adult vs. Adolescent
Teens need more sleep and have a shifted clock.
NSDR Protocol
Non-Sleep Deep Rest (or Yoga Nidra). 10-20 minutes immediately post-study accelerates learning and restores dopamine.
Lie down on back.
Exhale longer than inhale.
Mental body scan (focus on sensation).
Do not look at phone/screens.
Vestibular Reset
Taking a walk or bike ride (forward motion) after studying generates "optic flow," which quiets the amygdala and helps lock in memory.

FlickFleet is the public App Store release of the project originally developed as Paper Fleet Duel. Use this page to download the game, report a problem, suggest an improvement, or find help.
Available on the Apple App Store
FlickFleet App Store version 1.0 has been approved for iOS and is publicly available.
Download FlickFleet
Report an issue
For bugs and reproducible game problems, open a GitHub issue. Please check the issue carefully before submitting because GitHub issue reports are public.
Open a GitHub Issue Email Support
When reporting a problem, include the game version, iPhone model, iOS version, game mode, AI difficulty, what happened, what you expected, and the steps needed to make it happen again. A screenshot is helpful when it does not contain private information.
Common questions
The other player or AI does not receive a turn
Wait for the attack line and ship movement animation to finish. If control does not pass to the next captain, record the game mode, difficulty, current level and the last action taken, then submit an issue using the button above.
My flick did not travel in the direction I expected
The shot direction is taken from the first instant of finger movement and is locked after launch. Begin with your finger on your own half, then make one clean movement toward the opposing fleet. Starting farther from the centre line produces more force.
Why did a ship move during an attack?
Ships may move inside their assigned waters while an attack is underway. Some ships remain anchored on a turn. Moving ships travel from their visible bow, and larger ships turn more slowly than small craft.
Why does the HUD sometimes hide or reduce itself?
The interface adapts to the current game state. Unavailable bonuses can be hidden, and HUD elements may minimise around ships to keep the play area clear.
Where are names, levels, credits and scores stored?
Player names, the AI name, campaign progress, credits, fleet purchases and high scores are stored locally on the iPhone. FlickFleet does not require a Know & Guide account.
Will deleting the game remove my progress?
Deleting the app normally removes its local data. Some information may remain in an Apple device or iCloud backup depending on your backup settings.
Release status
FlickFleet is now a released iPhone game rather than a private prototype. Development continues, so gameplay balance, fleet movement, AI difficulty, progression and interface details may still improve in future updates.

Learning Intent: Calculate Cylinder SA and justify measurement accuracy.
Cylinder Formula
A cylinder consists of two circles and one "rolled" rectangle.
$$TSA = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh$$
Where $2\pi rh$ is the Curved Surface Area.
Percentage Error
Used to see how close an estimate is to the real value.
$$\% Error = \left| \frac{Approx - Exact}{Exact} \right| \times 100$$

Starfall Interceptor Support
Use this page to find help with Starfall Interceptor, report a reproducible problem, or review release and privacy information. The Apple bundle identifier is com.knowandguide.StarfallInterceptor.
Available on the Apple App Store
StarfallInterceptor version 1.0 has been approved for iOS and is publicly available from Apple.
Download StarfallInterceptor
Report an issue
For bugs and reproducible game problems, open a GitHub issue or email support. GitHub issues are public, so do not include passwords, private contact details or other sensitive information.
Open a GitHub Issue Email Support
When reporting a problem, include the game version, iPhone or iPad model, iOS/iPadOS version, game mode, planet and level, what happened, what you expected and the steps needed to make it happen again. A screenshot is helpful when it does not contain private information.
Common questions
What is the aim of Starfall Interceptor?
The hostile ships are under mind control by The Veil. The player's SoulHeal laser is designed to liberate controlled pilots rather than simply destroy them. When a ship is fully liberated it becomes harmless, changes to its liberation state and leaves the battle.
How do Beginner, Normal and Expert differ?
Beginner begins with the training levels and uses the gentlest speed and aggression curve. Normal starts later with full standard movement speed and stronger aggression. Expert increases movement and combat tempo further for experienced players.
Can I swap the joystick and fire controls?
Yes. Pause the game and choose Swap Controls. The joystick and FIRE/HYPER control cluster change sides for left- or right-handed play, and the preference is saved locally.
How do ship upgrades work?
Star Credits are earned by playing. They can be used for persistent ship upgrades such as shield capacity, shield regeneration, laser capability, engine thrust and Hyperdrive cooling. These gameplay upgrades are earned in the game rather than purchased with payment-card information.
What happens when I lose all lives?
After the final life is lost, the current run ends and Starfall Interceptor returns to the pilot-mode selection screen so you can choose Beginner, Normal or Expert for the next run.
Can I turn the background music off?
Yes. Pause the game and turn Music off. This silences the background soundtrack while leaving lasers, impacts, Hyperdrive and alien liberation voices available.
Where are scores, achievements and upgrades stored?
Starfall Interceptor stores game progress locally on the device. This includes scores, career progress, medals, achievements, Star Credits, upgrades, settings and save/checkpoint information. A Know & Guide account is not required.
What happens at the end of the current campaign?
The campaign spans three worlds. After completing the frontier of the current campaign, the ending screen allows the player to restart and choose a different skill level while retaining accumulated score and persistent ship abilities.
Will deleting the game remove my progress?
Deleting the app normally removes locally stored Starfall Interceptor data. Some information may remain in an Apple device or iCloud backup depending on your backup settings.
Privacy
Starfall Interceptor does not require a Know & Guide account and the current version does not include third-party advertising or analytics. Read the full policy for details about locally stored progress and support communications.

resources.text:
Know & Guide arcade game • now on the App Store STARFALL
INTERCEPTOR Liberate the pilots. Defend the worlds. Break The Veil.
Starfall Interceptor
Starfall Interceptor is a fast 2D arcade space game for iPhone and iPad. It takes the feel of classic horizontal space shooters and rebuilds it around a different idea: the alien pilots attacking your world are not the true enemy. They are being controlled by a hidden force known as The Veil.
Now available on the Apple App Store.
Apple approved StarfallInterceptor version 1.0 for iOS in August 2026. Download the released game directly from the App Store.
Download StarfallInterceptor
The mission is liberation, not conquest.
The player's SoulHeal laser breaks the control placed on enemy pilots. A fully liberated ship stops attacking, changes into its peaceful liberation state and leaves the battle. The campaign begins on your own planet, follows the control signal to the first mothership, and then carries the fight to other worlds that are also trapped under The Veil.
Core gameplay
Centred flight modelThe player ship stays near the centre while forward and reverse joystick pressure changes the speed of the world moving underneath it.
SoulHeal weaponsStarter fire begins as a deliberate single shot and develops through upgrades into stronger burst and rapid-fire capability.
Living enemy AISmall ships regroup and try to survive, larger ships behave more independently, and enemies attack both the player and settlements.
People and citiesCivilians and buildings follow the terrain, cities can be attacked and damaged, and protecting the planet matters to score and progression.
Multipart mothershipsBoss encounters are physical structures with independently liberatable systems, blocked lines of fire, changing attack patterns and different world-specific designs.
Three play stylesBeginner, Normal and Expert change the speed and aggression of the campaign so players can replay at a different challenge level.
Persistent pilot careerScores, ranks, achievements, medals, Star Credits and ship upgrades build over time and remain part of the player's career.
Accessible controlsThe pause menu can swap joystick and FIRE/HYPER sides for left- or right-handed play.
Dynamic soundtrackCalm and battle music crossfade according to threat level, with dedicated music logic for major mothership encounters.
Campaign structure
The campaign contains three worlds and thirty numbered levels. World 1 introduces the liberation mechanic and ends with the first horizontal mothership. World 2 introduces an industrial fortress fleet and a very different upright mothership. World 3 combines returning enemy families in new colours and escalating formations before the current campaign reaches its frontier ending.
After the current campaign is completed, the player can restart and choose a different difficulty while retaining accumulated score and persistent ship abilities.
Designed for local play
Starfall Interceptor does not require a Know & Guide account. Game progress, scores, achievements, Star Credits, upgrades, saves and settings are stored locally on the device. The current release does not include third-party advertising or analytics.

Tarot Quest Privacy Policy

Plain-language summary
Tarot Quest does not require an account, does not contain advertising, and does not use third-party analytics. Learning progress, settings, and journal entries are stored locally on your iPhone. Optional spoken-practice features use Apple-provided microphone and speech-recognition services.
1. Information stored on your device
Tarot Quest may store the following information locally on your iPhone:
learning progress, XP, levels, coins, streaks, and achievements;
voice preference and voice-speed settings;
saved tarot readings, interpretations, and journal entries; and
other app preferences needed to operate the learning experience.
This information is used only to provide the app’s features. Know & Guide does not operate a Tarot Quest user-account system or a remote journal database.
2. Microphone and speech recognition
Tarot Quest requests microphone and speech-recognition permission only when you choose spoken reading practice. Apple’s Speech framework may process speech on the device or through Apple services, depending on the device, language, and iOS configuration. Know & Guide does not receive or retain your voice recordings or speech transcripts through a separate server.
You can deny or withdraw these permissions at any time in iPhone Settings → Privacy & Security. The rest of the app remains available without spoken practice.
3. Information we do not collect through the app
The current version of Tarot Quest does not include:
third-party advertising;
third-party analytics or tracking SDKs;
location tracking;
contact-list access;
a user login or account profile; or
in-app purchases or payment-card collection.
Purchases and downloads are handled by Apple through the App Store under Apple’s own privacy and payment terms.
4. Support communications
If you contact support by email, we receive the information you choose to include, such as your email address, device details, screenshots, and problem description. This information is used to respond to your request and troubleshoot the app. Do not send private journal entries, passwords, financial information, or other sensitive information.
5. Data deletion
You can delete individual journal entries inside the app where that option is available. Deleting Tarot Quest from your iPhone removes the app’s locally stored data unless it is preserved by an Apple device backup. Backup retention and deletion are controlled through your Apple and iCloud settings.
6. Children’s privacy
Tarot Quest is a general educational and entertainment app and is not designed to collect personal information from children. The app does not require an account and does not knowingly collect children’s personal information through a Know & Guide server.

Experimental browser feature
Find your way with AI tools
Know & Guide offers three WebMCP tools that let a compatible AI assistant search our public resources, read their indexed content, and open a page for you.
Browser support
WebMCP is a proposed standard and remains experimental. These tools appear only in a supporting browser with WebMCP enabled and an agent that can use it. The website works normally in other browsers.
Chrome offers an origin trial from version 149 and a local testing flag at chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing. This site has no origin-trial token configured, so use an enabled testing browser to try it. Follow the current Chrome WebMCP setup guide for availability and the Model Context Tool Inspector extension.
What your assistant can do
Find a resource
search_knowandguide_resources searches learning material, blog posts, research, apps, support, privacy, projects, and information about Know & Guide.
Try: “Find Year 9 maths lessons on Know & Guide.”
Read public content
get_knowandguide_resource returns a resource’s indexed text. Longer resources can be read in sections. The index is a snapshot of published content, so open the page when you need its full layout, media, or interactive features.
Try: “Read the Paper Fleet Duel support information.”
Open a page
open_knowandguide_resource navigates this tab to a page in our public resource catalogue on the same website.
Try: “Open that lesson for me.”
Public resources, a clear scope
These tools use only our public content catalogue. They do not access admin data, read form entries, submit forms, or perform account actions. They do not control separate apps hosted on Know & Guide subdomains.
The WebMCP integration does not add an AI service, API key, or query analytics. Searching and reading the downloaded catalogue happen in your browser. Your chosen browser, assistant, or inspector may process requests under its own privacy settings.
For developers: try the native API
For Chrome 155 and later with WebMCP enabled, open developer tools on this site and run the following after the page loads. See the official imperative API guide for current syntax.
const tools = await document.modelContext.getTools(); const search = tools.find( tool => tool.name === "search_knowandguide_resources" ); const args = { query: "Year 9 maths", category: "learning", limit: 5 }; await document.modelContext.executeTool(search, args);
In Chrome 153–154, use await document.modelContext.executeTool(search, JSON.stringify(args)) for the last line.
The integration also recognises earlier implementations using navigator.modelContext. Browser APIs and inspector support can change while WebMCP is experimental.
